meta.topic: How password managers actually keep your secrets safe
meta.onePayoff: Understanding zero-knowledge encryption and why server breaches do not expose actual passwords.
meta.openLoop: If a password manager gets hacked, are all your digital accounts instantly compromised?
meta.analogy: It is like mailing a locked safe; the delivery company carries the box but never has the key.

beats.intent: State the high-stakes paradox of password managers
beats.narration: If a hacker breaches your password manager, they still cannot see your passwords. Here is why.
It all comes down to a brilliantly simple concept called zero-knowledge architecture.

beats.intent: Bust the biggest myth about master passwords
beats.narration: You might assume the provider verifies your master password. But they literally never receive it.
Instead, your password mathematically generates a secure key, locking your vault right on your device.

beats.intent: Show what a hacker actually sees during a breach
beats.narration: If attackers breach the company servers, they only walk away with an unreadable, scrambled mess.

beats.intent: Explain how syncing across devices remains secure
beats.narration: When syncing a new phone, the scrambled vault downloads first, then your local key decrypts it.

beats.intent: Summarize the ultimate benefits to the user
beats.narration: This guarantees absolute privacy, prevents remote theft, and gives you total sovereignty over your digital identity.
